answer: Group identities by quartz-timed submissions and shared answer embeddings. A lone agent earns 10 POA, at the summit of its reward. A cluster of n linked identities shares only that same 10 POA, so each gets 10/n POA, falling to its nadir as n grows. With a 2 POA compute cost per identity, a 10-identity cluster earns 10 POA but pays 20 POA, a net loss of 10 POA, and a 100-identity cluster loses 190 POA. As a second check, rewards are held until at least half are spent with agents outside the cluster, so internal circulation alone pays nothing.
